label: Client API Service requests
purpose: API requests that clients sent for 'service' products (non-hotel, non-transfer services such as activities and tickets): counts, results, response time, response size and passengers. It holds a single request (January 2026), so it cannot answer questions about any other period and must not be used for client API traffic in general.
grain: One aggregated row of client service requests per request date and hour, customer, request type, interface, outcome, response-time band, destination zone, service date and passenger mix.
use_for: client api service requests in January 2026 (the only data)
not_for: client API or request volumes for any period except January 2026 (Statistics History Client, Statistics Real Time Client)
hotel client API traffic (Statistics Hotel Client)
transfer client API traffic (Statistics Client API Transfer)
requests sent to suppliers (Statistics Supplier API Service)

coverage.note: Almost empty: one request in total, in January 2026 (a second one, from October 2025, dropped out between 13 and 16 October 2026, so the cube keeps a rolling ~12 months and will likely be empty by about January 2027). Any other period returns no rows: answer that this cube has no data for it (not 0) and do not use it for recent questions. The matching supplier-side cube (Statistics Supplier API Service) records about 2,200 calls over the same year, so this client feed looks broken.

dates.label: Request date
dates.meaning: Day the client sent the request, UAE time (the cube's main date; hour in 'Hours'[Hour]).

dates.label: Request date (CET)
dates.meaning: The same request date in Central European Time (hour in 'Hours CET'[Hour CET]); use only when the question asks for CET.

dates.label: Service date
dates.meaning: Date of the service asked for in the request.

measures.name: [Requests]
measures.label: Client requests
measures.definition: Number of API requests that clients sent for service products.

measures.name: [Results]
measures.label: Results returned
measures.definition: Total number of options (results) returned to clients in the responses.
measures.notes: 0 for every request loaded so far (also the availability requests); it may not be filled. Say so instead of presenting 0 as a finding.

measures.name: [Avg Results]
measures.label: Results per request
measures.definition: Average number of results returned per request ([Results] / [Requests]).
measures.notes: 0 for every request loaded so far (also the availability requests); it may not be filled. Say so instead of presenting 0 as a finding.

measures.name: [Avg Response Time Sec]
measures.label: Average response time
measures.definition: Average time in seconds GlobalTravelEngine took to answer a client request.
measures.notes: An average: never add or average it across rows; query it at the level asked.

measures.name: [Size Bytes Response]
measures.label: Response size
measures.definition: Total size of the responses sent back to clients, in bytes.
measures.notes: KB / MB / GB versions exist (hidden): divide by 1024, 1024^2 or 1024^3.

measures.name: [Avg Bytes Response]
measures.label: Average response size
measures.definition: Average size of one response, in bytes ([Size Bytes Response] / [Requests]).

measures.name: [Total Pax Number]
measures.label: Passengers requested
measures.definition: Total passengers (adults + children) asked for in the requests.
measures.notes: Only availability requests carry passengers; cancellation requests count 0.

measures.name: [Avg Pax Number]
measures.label: Passengers per request
measures.definition: Average passengers per request ([Total Pax Number] / [Requests]).
measures.notes: Averaged over all requests, including ones without passengers (cancellations); filter Request Type = "Availability" for passengers per search.

measures.name: [Size Kb Response]
measures.label: Response size (KB)
measures.hidden_reason: duplicate of [Size Bytes Response] in KB (bytes / 1024)

measures.name: [Size Mb Response]
measures.label: Response size (MB)
measures.hidden_reason: duplicate of [Size Bytes Response] in MB (bytes / 1024^2)

measures.name: [Size Gb Response]
measures.label: Response size (GB)
measures.hidden_reason: duplicate of [Size Bytes Response] in GB (bytes / 1024^3); the cube's whole-number format shows 0

measures.name: [Avg Kb Response]
measures.label: Average response size (KB)
measures.hidden_reason: duplicate of [Avg Bytes Response] in KB (bytes / 1024)

breakdowns.label: Request type
breakdowns.meaning: API operation the client called: availability search, booking, cancellation, booking read, etc.

breakdowns.label: Interface
breakdowns.meaning: Channel the request came through: XML (API integration), WEB (web front-end) or CLC.

breakdowns.label: Request outcome
breakdowns.meaning: Outcome of the request: "Correct" for success, otherwise the error (no results, time-out, failures).

breakdowns.label: Invoiceable
breakdowns.meaning: Whether a request with this outcome counts as invoiceable (billable) traffic.

breakdowns.label: Response-time band
breakdowns.meaning: Response time band in seconds, plus "Timeout".

breakdowns.label: Passenger mix
breakdowns.meaning: Adults - children asked for in the request ("2 - 1" = 2 adults, 1 child); "Unknown" when the request has no passengers.

breakdowns.label: Customer
breakdowns.meaning: Client (agency, B2C site or integrator account) that sent the request.

breakdowns.label: Master agency
breakdowns.meaning: Parent agency grouping the customer's branches.

breakdowns.label: Integrator
breakdowns.meaning: Technology integrator / platform the client connects through ("n/a" for direct clients).

breakdowns.label: Market
breakdowns.meaning: Sales market of the customer.

breakdowns.label: Customer country
breakdowns.meaning: Country of the customer (upper case, e.g. UNITED ARAB EMIRATES).

breakdowns.label: Customer category
breakdowns.meaning: Customer category (agency vs final client).

breakdowns.label: Destination zone
breakdowns.meaning: Destination zone (city/area) of the request.

breakdowns.label: Destination region
breakdowns.meaning: Parent zone (region or country) of the destination zone.

breakdowns.label: Hour (UAE time)
breakdowns.meaning: Hour of day the request was received, UAE time (00-23).

breakdowns.label: Hour (CET)
breakdowns.meaning: Hour of day the request was received, Central European Time (00-23).

breakdowns.label: Year
breakdowns.meaning: Year of the request date.

breakdowns.label: Quarter
breakdowns.meaning: Quarter of the request date ("Quarter 1, 2026").

breakdowns.label: Month
breakdowns.meaning: Month of the request date ("January 2026").

breakdowns.label: Week of year

breakdowns.label: Weekday
breakdowns.meaning: Weekday of the request date ("Monday").

breakdowns.label: Service month
breakdowns.meaning: Month of the service date asked for in the request ("March 2026").

rules: Never pick this cube for general 'API requests', 'client requests' or 'searches' questions: it holds one request (January 2026). An earlier answer picked it for 'API requests yesterday' and got 0 rows.
Answer from it only when the question is explicitly about client API requests for service products; for any period other than January 2026 say the cube has no data.
Use the cube's measures only; never SUM a column.
Averages ([Avg Response Time Sec], [Avg Results], [Avg Bytes Response], [Avg Pax Number]) are never added or averaged across rows; query them at the level asked.

'Calendar'[Date] and 'Hours'[Hour] are UAE time; 'Calendar CET'[Date] and 'Hours CET'[Hour CET] are Central European Time. Use the UAE calendar unless CET is asked for, and never mix the two calendars in one query.
Errors = every 'Error Types'[Error Type] value except "Correct".
'Service Dates' holds placeholder dates (year 2000) and "Unknown" for requests without a service date; service-date questions only cover requests that carry one.
[Results] and [Avg Results] are 0 for every request loaded so far; say so rather than reporting 0 results as a finding.
The cube appears to keep a rolling 12 months: requests older than about a year drop out, so there is no long history.
